name: AR400
source: Wikipedia, 'Abrasion resistant steel' (hardness table citing Canale & Totten (eds.), Failure Analysis of Heat Treated Steel Components, ASM International, 2008) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abrasion_resistant_steel
notes: hardness_HB is the lower bound of the published 360-440 HB range. AR grades are defined by hardness, not by a single ASTM chemistry; use the mill certificate for design.

name: AR500
source: Wikipedia, 'Abrasion resistant steel' (hardness table citing Canale & Totten (eds.), Failure Analysis of Heat Treated Steel Components, ASM International, 2008) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abrasion_resistant_steel
notes: hardness_HB is the lower bound of the published 460-544 HB range. Source notes higher-BHN grades are more brittle.

name: Hadfield manganese steel
source: Metallographic.com, 'Hadfield manganese steel' (ASTM A128 Grade B-1) https://metallographic.com/materials/hadfield-manganese-steel
notes: hardness_HB is the as-cast value (~200 HB); surface work-hardens to >500 HB under impact and abrasion. impact_resistance rated high because the source describes work-hardening under impact.

name: Ni-Hard 4
source: Wilfley, 'NiHard 4' material sheet (ASTM A532 Class I Type D) https://wilfley.com/lit/materials/nihard-4-hard-iron.pdf
notes: hardness_HB is the lower bound of the published 600-655 HBN average hardness. Supplier figure, not the A532 minimum.

name: High-chromium white iron
typical_applications: crusher liners;chute liners;ball mill liners;lifter bars;slurry pumps;impellers
source: Penticton Foundry, 'Alloy data sheet: high chrome white iron 25%' (ASTM A532 Class III Type A) https://www.pentictonfoundry.com/news/alloy-data-sheet-25-high-chromium-alloy/
notes: hardness_HB is the lower bound of the hardened 600-700 HB range (as-cast 450-550; annealed 300-450; varies with section thickness). Density published as 7.6 g/cm3.

name: Alumina ceramic
notes: Brinell is not applicable to technical ceramics; source gives Knoop (1000 gf) 14.1 GPa and fracture toughness 4-5 MPa.m^0.5. Density published as 3.90 g/cm3. Lower-purity grades are less dense.

name: Natural rubber
notes: Hardness 60 +/- 5 Shore A (ASTM D2240); density 1.14 +/- 0.05 g/cm3 per product data. Max service temperature +70 C. Other NR wear compounds range widely (e.g. Weir Vulco R67 mill liner rubber is 65 Shore A).

name: Polyurethane
notes: General-purpose cast PU plate, not a mining-specific liner grade. Hardness 90 +/- 5 Shore A; density 1.26 g/cm3; working range -40 to +80 C.
